6.speaker: Marcel Koronti
6.text: “I'm sure you'll agree that the support I and my network have given your administration has been nothing but beneficial."

7.speaker: Marcel Koronti
7.text: “Mr. Rayne. I used my connections to cancel the publishing of 73 negative articles and personally directed the release of more than 41 positive reports, be they on the television, radio or newsprint.”

8.speaker: Marcel Koronti
8.text: “Half of the non-state media in the country has been sharing positive news about you and downplaying negative events.”

9.speaker: Marcel Koronti
9.text: “I'm glad you agree. Your public opinion could have nosedived were it not for us.”

10.speaker: Marcel Koronti
10.text: “Out of goodwill, I will share a key piece of information.”

11.speaker: Player
11.text: “I don't see why we should be enemies.”

12.speaker: Marcel Koronti
12.text: “You can't blame them, can you? Imagine someone trying to take your authority and personal wealth away without your consent.”

13.speaker: Player
13.text: “We will only ask for a reasonable share. Nothing out of the ordinary.”

14.speaker: Player
14.text: “They'll have to deal with whatever I decide. It is a tough world.”

15.speaker: Marcel Koronti
15.text: “I can't help but mention the tax breaks, Mr. President.”
15.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn02_InT_Corporation_UnderhallConstruction"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxBreak_LargeCorporations"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Economy_BusinessBailout"] == true) == false)

16.speaker: Player
16.text: “I haven't been seeing any benefits yet.”

17.speaker: Player
17.text: "There's always more you could be doing for us.”

18.speaker: Marcel Koronti
18.text: “Please don't take what I'm about to say as a threat.”

20.speaker: Player
20.text: “Our partnership has been successful so far.”

24.speaker: Marcel Koronti
24.text: “The increased taxes have made a substantial dent in HOS' net profits. This has hurt the backbone of the Sordish economy.”

25.speaker: Marcel Koronti
25.text: “Mr. Rayne. We essentially acquired Lachaven Times and have been coordinating media publishing across the three largest broadcasting organisations.”

29.speaker: Narrator
29.text: I heard him knock on wood.

30.speaker: Player
30.text: “I'm glad to hear that. It was a widely contested decision.”

32.speaker: Player
32.text: “Of course. Private corporations had to have a financial leg up to boost investments.”

33.speaker: Player
33.text: “Needless to say, I still expect you to reinvest any surplus back into the economy to create more jobs.”

34.speaker: Player
34.text: “Underhall has been a pleasure to work with. They made our opening a success."

35.speaker: Marcel Koronti
35.text: “Increasing our investments inside Sordland is a key topic in our board discussions.”

36.speaker: Player
36.text: “The decision wasn't necessarily made to benefit you, Marcel.”

37.speaker: Marcel Koronti
37.text: “We managed to avoid closing those companies, and they satisfied the Board of HOS with a high profit report in return.”

41.speaker: Narrator
41.text: He paused for a few seconds.
41.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxIncrease_LargeCorporations"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn02_InT_Corporation_UnderhallConstruction"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxBreak_LargeCorporations"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Economy_BusinessBailout"] == true) == false)

42.speaker: Marcel Koronti
42.text: “The mayor of Conriat Kris Schar is a close friend and an investor in Underhall, and your contracting of the firm has tripled his returns."

52.speaker: Narrator
52.text: I was in my office, looking through the agenda for the upcoming meeting at the Ministry of Economy.

54.speaker: Marcel Koronti
54.text: “Greetings, Mr. President. I'm sorry to disturb you before such an important meeting. But I thought now would be a good time to talk about our... arrangement."

55.speaker: Marcel Koronti
55.text: “Greetings, Mr. President. It has been a while, hasn't it?"

56.speaker: Marcel Koronti
56.text: “Let me try to remember. When was the last time we had a chat?”

57.speaker: Marcel Koronti
57.text: “Oh, I remember. It was in Conriat when you refused my gracious offer.”

58.speaker: Marcel Koronti
58.text: “Greetings, Mr. President. It has been a while, hasn't it?"

59.speaker: Marcel Koronti
59.text: “Let me try to remember. When was the last time we had a chat?”

60.speaker: Marcel Koronti
60.text: “Oh, I remember. It was when you refused to meet with me.”

61.speaker: Marcel Koronti
61.text: “And look at where we are now.”

62.speaker: Marcel Koronti
62.text: “Greetings, Mr. President. My name is Marcel Koronti. CEO of Heart of Sordland Enterprises.”

63.speaker: Marcel Koronti
63.text: “Unfortunately, we haven't had the pleasure to chat yet.”

65.speaker: Player
65.text: “I've been starting to regret that decision.”

67.speaker: Marcel Koronti
67.text: “Well, we are both adults here. I am sure we can let past be past and focus on the future.”

68.speaker: Marcel Koronti
68.text: “Although this time, I am talking about the short-term future...”

70.speaker: Marcel Koronti
70.text: “That is unfortunate. My father once had a saying—may he rest in peace.”

71.speaker: Marcel Koronti
71.text: “He told me that if I don't seize an opportunity when it is presented, the opportunity could disappear forever.”

72.speaker: Marcel Koronti
72.text: “And that's how I have chosen to live my life. Unlike you, it seems."

73.speaker: Marcel Koronti
73.text: “You probably know why I am calling. It's because of the upcoming ownership meeting.”

74.speaker: Marcel Koronti
74.text: “But before we move on to that...”

75.speaker: Player
75.text: “You tell me. Where are we now?”

77.speaker: Player
77.text: “I've been starting to regret that decision.”

78.speaker: Marcel Koronti
78.text: “The real question is about where *you* are. Not me.”

79.speaker: Marcel Koronti
79.text: “If we worked together, *you* could be so much more. *You* could've accomplished so much more.”

80.speaker: Marcel Koronti
80.text: “Yet you wouldn't even deign to meet with me.”

81.speaker: Marcel Koronti
81.text: “He told me that if I don't seize an opportunity when it is presented, the opportunity could disappear forever.”

82.speaker: Marcel Koronti
82.text: “That is unfortunate. My father once had a saying—may he rest in peace.”

83.speaker: Marcel Koronti
83.text: “And that's how I have chosen to live my life. Unlike you, it seems."

84.speaker: Marcel Koronti
84.text: “You probably know why I am calling. It's because of the upcoming ownership meeting.”

85.speaker: Marcel Koronti
85.text: “Anyway. That's not why I called. We are both adults here. I am sure we can let past be past and focus on the future.”

86.speaker: Marcel Koronti
86.text: “Although this time, I am talking about the more short-term future...”

88.speaker: Marcel Koronti
88.text: “But before we move on to that.”

89.speaker: Marcel Koronti
89.text: “My attempts to reach you seem to have failed every time, as if I was being... avoided.”

90.speaker: Player
90.text: “Get to the point. What do you want?”

92.speaker: Player
92.text: “Apologies. That was certainly not my intention.”

93.speaker: Marcel Koronti
93.text: “I think you know why I am calling.”

94.speaker: Marcel Koronti
94.text: “It's because of the upcoming ownership meeting.”

96.speaker: Marcel Koronti
96.text: “Although, of course, I would've liked it if we had a closer friendship.”

97.speaker: Marcel Koronti
97.text: “After all, there is no need to dwell on our previous missed opportunities.”

98.speaker: Marcel Koronti
98.text: “But no. That was not my real intention for calling you today.”

99.speaker: Marcel Koronti
99.text: “I'm calling you because of the upcoming ownership meeting.”

100.speaker: Marcel Koronti
100.text: “I think you already know. I'm calling because of the upcoming ownership meeting.”

102.speaker: Marcel Koronti
102.text: “My father once told me—may he rest in peace.”

103.speaker: Marcel Koronti
103.text: “He told me that if I don't seize an opportunity when it is presented, the opportunity could disappear forever.”

104.speaker: Marcel Koronti
104.text: “And that's how I have chosen to live my life. Unlike you, it seems."

105.speaker: Marcel Koronti
105.text: “But past is past. And we must look at the future. Specifically, the very short-term future.”

106.speaker: Marcel Koronti
106.text: “I'm talking about the upcoming ownership meeting.”

107.speaker: Marcel Koronti
107.text: “I wanted to thank you for choosing Underhall Construction to complete the H-3 highway."

109.speaker: Marcel Koronti
109.text: “It is the number-one construction company in Sordland, after all.”

110.speaker: Marcel Koronti
110.text: “Perhaps not, but it certainly worked out for me.”

111.speaker: Marcel Koronti
111.text: “Your business bailout greatly benefitted certain subsidiaries of HOS that were reporting record losses.”

112.speaker: Marcel Koronti
112.text: “I know it has been a while, but I have to give credit where it's due. Or overdue, in this case."

113.speaker: Marcel Koronti
113.text: “It must've been a hard choice. It is safe to say that you picked the right one.”

117.speaker: Marcel Koronti
117.text: “They have been extraordinarily beneficial to our quarterly performance. HOS is now operating on a much larger revenue pool."

118.speaker: Marcel Koronti
118.text: “You have successfully strengthened the backbone of the Sordish economy.”

120.speaker: Player
120.text: “It was a tough decision. Don't make me regret it.”

121.speaker: Marcel Koronti
121.text: “I can't help but mention your tax hike, Mr. President."
121.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxIncrease_LargeCorporations"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn02_InT_Corporation_UnderhallConstruction"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_EnT_TaxBreak_LargeCorporations"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Economy_BusinessBailout"] == true) == false)

124.speaker: Marcel Koronti
124.text: “That way of thinking is correct, but you acted wrongly. This will only serve to damage our economy in the long run.”

125.speaker: Player
125.text: “Unfortunately, we had to tighten our belts wherever we could.”

126.speaker: Marcel Koronti
126.text: “But I assure you, it is nothing we can't endure.”

127.speaker: Marcel Koronti
127.text: “The Lotherberg Group has contingency plans if you decide to do anything rash that would disrupt their empires.”

128.speaker: Marcel Koronti
128.text: “If you are not careful about what happens next, it might cost you dearly.”

130.speaker: Marcel Koronti
130.text: “If everyone plays their cards right, it will be all fine.”

132.speaker: Narrator
132.text: The phone rang and I put the agenda down.

133.speaker: Narrator
133.text: The meeting was going to be about the ownership of the Big Four, the four corporations at the heart of Sordland's ownership debate: Heart of Sordland, Bergia Steel, the Sordish State Corporation and Nedam Mining Group.
133.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn06_Lobbying_Bribe"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn06_Lobbying_Bribe2"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn06_Lobbying_Bribe3"] == true) == false

134.speaker: Narrator
134.text: Some of these companies were controlled in part or entirely by the state. The others were mostly or completely privatized. I had the power to change that fact.

135.speaker: Marcel Koronti
135.text: “Nobody in the entire country is supporting you as much as I am.”

141.speaker: Marcel Koronti
141.text: “Since the start of your campaign, you've adamantly promoted a planned economy."

142.speaker: Marcel Koronti
142.text: “Going by that, I am worried that you will attempt to nationalize Sordland's largest private corporations. Nationalization as a concept goes against everything my father built and stood for.”

143.speaker: Marcel Koronti
143.text: “If you do want to go down this road, I must insist on you excluding HOS from any such plan. That is my most important request."

147.speaker: Marcel Koronti
147.text: “You may recall that one of the terms of our agreement was that I may ask you for one favor. Well, this is it."

148.speaker: Marcel Koronti
148.text: “Think of your corporate allies as a sea of ravenous sharks surrounding you. We could co-exist peacefully, or..."

149.speaker: Marcel Koronti
149.text: “Ah, let's not even imagine that scenario.”

151.speaker: Player
151.text: “Imagine this scenario. You will either help me out, or I will eat your little company for dinner. Understood?”

152.speaker: Player
152.text: “I don't give in to threats. Your time is over, Koronti.”

153.speaker: Player
153.text: “Don't get your knickers in a twist. I was planning on leaving HOS alone anyway.”

155.speaker: Marcel Koronti
155.text: “What an unfortunate turn of events. What a tragedy!”

156.speaker: Marcel Koronti
156.text: “When I'm done with you, getting re-elected will be the least of your worries, Mr. *President*.”

157.speaker: Marcel Koronti
157.text: “Listen to me. Do you think you have power because you're sitting in the fancy chair? Do you think you are Soll?”

158.speaker: Marcel Koronti
158.text: “If you want war, you will have your war. But know this.”

161.speaker: Marcel Koronti
161.text: “I knew we would be on the same page!”

162.speaker: Marcel Koronti
162.text: “I am raising my glass to you right now, Mr. President.”

163.speaker: Marcel Koronti
163.text: “There is actually one more thing I would like to discuss.”

164.speaker: Marcel Koronti
164.text: “As long as you do as I say and exclude my *little* company, I will gladly help you.”

165.speaker: Marcel Koronti
165.text: “I always keep my end of the bargain, Mr. President. Don't forget.”

166.speaker: Marcel Koronti
166.text: “You had better keep yours as well.”

167.speaker: Marcel Koronti
167.text: “Before we end the call, there is actually one more thing I would like to discuss.”

169.speaker: Marcel Koronti
169.text: “As long as we both understand what entails *not* being enemies.”

171.speaker: Marcel Koronti
171.text: “Since the start of your campaign, you've wisely committed to a market economy."

172.speaker: Marcel Koronti
172.text: “Judging by that, I am sure you are looking into privatizing some of the companies that are currently state owned.”

173.speaker: Marcel Koronti
173.text: “I believe, therefore, that privatizing both Nedam Mining Group and the Sordish State Corporation would be in both of our interests.”

175.speaker: Marcel Koronti
175.text: “I will destroy you and everything you hold dear.”

178.speaker: Marcel Koronti
178.text: “After all, I am considering buying stocks in both companies.”

181.speaker: Marcel Koronti
181.text: “Be careful around the people you trust.”

185.speaker: Marcel Koronti
185.text: “Excellent! Great minds do think alike. Thank you for your support.”

186.speaker: Player
186.text: “Privatizing both might be too much. I will see what I can do.”

187.speaker: Marcel Koronti
187.text: “Think about it this way. It is another step forward in strengthening our economy.”

190.speaker: Marcel Koronti
190.text: “What do you mean? You will leave everything the same, then?”

191.speaker: Marcel Koronti
191.text: “Don't tell me you are thinking about nationalization?”

193.speaker: Marcel Koronti
193.text: “Mr. President. Nationalization as a concept goes against everything my father built and stood for.”

194.speaker: Player
194.text: “I'm thinking about a more balanced approach.”

195.speaker: Marcel Koronti
195.text: “Balance is important, Mr. President, but the concept of nationalization goes against everything my father built and stood for.”

198.speaker: Marcel Koronti
198.text: “Before we end the call, there is actually one more thing I would like to discuss.”

202.speaker: Marcel Koronti
202.text: “Mr. Tusk is unfit to be the spokesperson for the Lotherberg Group. His archaic thinking has only preserved a status quo that benefits himself and precious few others."

205.speaker: Player
205.text: “Who do you have in mind to replace him?”

206.speaker: Player
206.text: “Stop. Before you say anything more, I won't meddle in Oligarchs' affairs.”

207.speaker: Marcel Koronti
207.text: “Ah, it was worth a shot. But I respect your decision.”

212.speaker: Marcel Koronti
212.text: “I have taken up enough of your time today.”

213.speaker: Marcel Koronti
213.text: “Here is what I propose. A win-win situation.”

214.speaker: Marcel Koronti
214.text: “It is time the group had a proper leader."

216.speaker: Marcel Koronti
216.text: “If you could use your powers to make Bergia Steel, Tusk's main company, state-owned, he would lose considerable influence.”

218.speaker: Marcel Koronti
218.text: “If I take over with your help, I will be forever indebted to you and support you in all your goals, be they re-election or something more.”
218.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Accepted_MediaDeal"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn07_MarcelFavor_NoNationalizeHOS"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn07_MarcelFavor_PrivateTakeover"] == false) == false

222.speaker: Player
222.text: “I won't make myself a target by picking a side.”

224.speaker: Marcel Koronti
224.text: “Just think about it. That's all I am asking.”

225.speaker: Marcel Koronti
225.text: “You and me. We would be unstoppable. We could eliminate everyone who's after us.”

228.speaker: Marcel Koronti
228.text: “Thank you for your time, Mr. President.”

232.speaker: Narrator
232.text: After a couple of minutes, I went back to reviewing the agenda.

239.speaker: Marcel Koronti
239.text: “If you promised me a majority of shares from the privatization, he would lose considerable power.”

242.speaker: Player
242.text: “You've outlived your usefulness to me. You are done for, Koronti.”

243.speaker: Player
243.text: “I understand. I want our partnership to continue uninterrupted.”

249.speaker: Marcel Koronti
249.text: “You may recall that one of the terms of our agreement was that I may ask you for one favor. Well, this is it."

250.speaker: Marcel Koronti
250.text: “I want him gone. And you're going to make it happen."

259.speaker: Marcel Koronti
259.text: "Think about all the free help you've gotten from me -- and the many scandals you might have to cover up on the way to re-election."

260.speaker: Marcel Koronti
260.text: "Korontis always keep their word, my father said. He would have liked you."

264.speaker: Marcel Koronti
264.text: “I wanted to thank you for choosing Underhall Construction to complete the L-1 railway."
